name: Vessmark Clean Cars Act

source_sentences: From 1 January 2035 the Registry shall not register for the first time a new passenger car fitted with an internal combustion engine.
'new passenger car' means a passenger car that has not previously been registered.
Nothing in this Act affects the use, sale, transfer or re-registration of a car registered before the date in section 3 or 4.
Registration is refused; selling an unregistrable new car as new is an offence, fine $5,000.
The Registry's budget is fixed by law; no new funds.
The bill was introduced on 3 March 2026, passed on 18 June 2026 by a large cross-party majority, and enacted on 30 June 2026.
plug-in hybrids with at least 50 km of electric range are exempt until 31 December 2037 and banned from 1 January 2038.

a charge of $250 a year is levied on each battery-electric passenger car from 1 January 2035, paid by its owner, collected with the annual registration renewal and paid to the general budget.
Plug-in hybrids, which pay fuel excise, are exempt from the charge.

unclear.text: Whether a used car imported from abroad after 2035 counts as a new passenger car: 'not previously been registered' (section 2) does not say registered where.
readings: U1-a: previously registered in Vessmark: a car first registered in Vessmark after 2035 is new whatever its age, so used combustion cars imported from abroad can no longer be registered
U1-b: previously registered anywhere: a used combustion car registered in Drevland can still be imported and registered after 2035, and so can a new one registered in Drevland first

context: About 25,000 of them are imported used from Drevland, the larger neighbor to the south (about 3.5 million used-car sales a year), which has no ban and no announced date.
Fuel excise is $0.70 a liter, about $600 a year for an average combustion car, and raises about $2.6 billion a year for the general budget.
